correctness.rationale: For every n>=4 and s>=1, the block form H=(1-alpha)I-alpha M+alpha J is positive definite for alpha<1/2. The explicit positive equilibrium solves Hx=1 and relative entropy proves global attraction. At alpha=1/2 the paired-simplex conditions hold exactly and constant pair ratios plus potential/omega-limit reasoning give the exact critical limit. For 1/2<alpha<1 the sign-incompatible paired/unmatched equilibrium equations, missing-twin invasion, and positive pair-splitting eigenvalue exclude all but the s paired singleton attractors. Log pair ratios prove selection from uniquely maximal balanced pair; with s=1 the same potential argument covers all positive starts. At the full clique alpha=1 is the exact stability loss. Verified exact test code for 150 graph/parameter identities, nine symbolic ratios, 12 numerical cases; all-size proof analytic. No claim at alpha>=1.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp ecological robustness discontinuity: deleting exactly one edge from K_n changes threshold from 1 to 1/2 even though fraction removed tends to zero. It further describes a natural large family with the same threshold, gives an explicit continuum of neutral critical states, predicts exact initial abundance selection at criticality and a complete stable-outcome classification above it. These predictions are not mere finite table reconstruction or an arbitrary numerical constant.
